title: Jonah and the Bakery
premise: Freya Whitlock, a marine biologist hiding from a career-destroying scandal, takes a winter job cataloging sea turtles near a struggling coastal vineyard and bakery run by the found-family crew of Harbor Lane. When a snowstorm traps her with Jonah Reyes—the rival scientist whose testimony ended her old life—old wounds and unexpected tenderness force both to confront how survival made them complicit in each other's ruin. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches, the corrupt investor threatening the bakery offers Freya her reputation back in exchange for betraying the people who took her in. She refuses, exposes him with Jonah's help, and chooses love and community over the safe invisibility she once believed was all she deserved.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who writes romances about people who mistake solitude for safety. She lives on a foggy coastline with an opinionated cat and a sourdough starter older than most of her relationships.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Arriving at Harbor Lane under a false name, Freya buries herself in turtle counts while dodging the warmth of the bakery crew who keep leaving bread at her door. When Jonah walks into the bakery—her rival, her ruin—she nearly flees. Emotional beat: guarded isolation cracked open by unwanted recognition.

chapters.title: What the Snow Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A blizzard strands Freya and Jonah alone overnight; flour-dusted confessions reveal he testified to save his own career and has regretted it ever since. They almost bridge the gap between them before morning shame pulls them apart. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered, then retreated from.

chapters.title: The Investor's Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The investor bankrolling the vineyard recognizes Freya and offers to restore her reputation if she'll falsify environmental reports that would sink the bakery. Torn, she watches the found family plan their first harvest, realizing what betrayal would cost. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by belonging.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the harvest festival, Freya publicly exposes the investor's fraud with evidence Jonah risked his career to secure; the community rallies, the deal collapses, and he asks for a real second chance—not forgiveness on credit. Freya stays, wholehearted at last. Emotional beat: redemption earned through courage, not timing.
